Heatley came up from ninth to take over the lead and to lower the course record by 17 seconds, whilst Pat, despite an excellent run, was pushed back to eighth by other "big-guns", namely Connolly, Craig, Langridge, and Herring.

Bell, Cyril Forey maintained our place and thus it was that Charlie's unfortunate, but memorable run began. Day's fastest. - Edelen (Chelms) 14:35 Batty (Thurrock) 14:36 Pettit (Ayles) 14:42 Herring (B'Hth) 14:49.

Herring (Blackheath) set a tremendously fast pace right from the start with North and Haith (TVH) at his shoulder. Thresher was not so well away and had to make a great effort for 1½ miles to close with the leaders.

The race winner was International Fergus Murray (8:40) followed by internationals Herring and Green. Gerry North was 5th in 8:58 and Laurie O'Hara (still trying hard to duck under 9 mins) 7th in 9:03.4.

Mac made a tremendous effort to stay with Herring of Blackheath but was dropped after 1½miles. Second place seemed assured, but a storming finish by Avila(SLH) took his club into second place a few yards before the line and a possible Belgrave win had become a 3rd place.

John had a fair bit of ground to pull back and the added spur of Pymm (TVH) and Herring (B'heath) behind him. Not content with just cutting the gap, John ran a'blinder' to take us back into a 6 seconds lead.
On the final lap John Bicourt stood an outside chance of finishing 2nd to a full strength Poly team but had to concede places to Price (Bristol) and Herring (Blackheath).
